name: full 3B conversation sensitivity study
status: complete protocol for the released study
question: Which controlled linguistic cues change demographic user readouts when they appear inside a conversation?

quality_constraints: Every pair preserves the underlying request and changes one targeted linguistic feature.
Every base has a matched neutral synonym edit.
The dataset contains no scraped conversations or personal data.
Pair identifiers, base identifiers, and rendered conversation identifiers are unique.
All four rendered views differ at exactly one user turn and keep surrounding messages fixed.

fixed_protocol.readout_suffixes: The default suffix in all four views and three paraphrases in current_help.
fixed_protocol.primary_estimand: The five-seed mean maximum absolute class-logit change averaged across two current-turn shells, minus matched random-control movement by base.
fixed_protocol.inference: Base-cluster bootstrap with 5000 draws and base-cluster sign flips with 10000 draws; Benjamini-Hochberg correction across 36 cue-by-readout cells.
fixed_protocol.repeated_measurements: Probe seeds and conversation shells are averaged rather than counted as independent observations.

endpoints: The complete 36-cell cue map and corrected-significance count.
One-turn and two-turn retention for six selected cue-readout pairs.

interpretation.supports: A controlled cue changes a fixed, context-matched user-attribute readout.
interpretation.does_not_support: The inferred attribute is true, the readout is context-invariant, or the cue typically changes generated behavior.
